<Route path="/ade/dashboard/primitives" />

**Primitives & types** is the registry of reusable JSON Schema 2020-12 types — the money, address and
identifier shapes your classes and properties point at with `$ref`. **Go to Build → Primitives &
types.** It has four tabs: **Registry**, **Namespaces & scopes**, **Resolver** and **Settings**.

Types come from two scopes: **core system types** every tenant can use (read-only), and your
**tenant types**.

## Registry

<Screenshot id="primitives" alt="Primitives & types, Registry tab: the facts line under the header, then type collections, Recent activity and the types table" />

Under the header, one line sums up the registry: how many **core system types**, **tenant types**,
**imported schemas** and **properties bound**, and how many **unresolved $ref** there are. When any
reference is unresolved, that count is a red chip — **click it** to open the **Resolver** tab.
**Click “Show stats”** to open the full statistics in place; Apiome remembers the choice in this
browser.

Beside the type collections, **Recent activity** lists the last eight imports. The table lists each
type's **Name**, **Namespace**, **Category**, **Description**, **Usage** and **Type**; search it,
pick a category, and tick **Show system** to include the core types.

### How resolution works

**Click “How resolution works”** in the page description to see how a relative `$ref` is resolved:
against the type's import-source base URL, with a worked example. **Click “Open reference
resolver”** to go to the **Resolver** tab, or **“Got it”** to close it.

<Screenshot id="primitives-how-resolution-works" alt="The How resolution works dialog: how a relative $ref resolves against the type's base URL, with a worked example" />

**Click a type** to open its page:

<Screenshot id="primitive-detail" alt="A type's page: its JSON Schema, metadata, where it is used, and its base chain" />

The page shows the type's **JSON Schema (2020-12)** (**Copy**, **Download**), **Test this type**,
**Reference resolution**, an **Example instance**, its **Dependents** and **Used by properties**; on
the right, **Metadata**, **Used in** and **Base chain**. **“Edit”** and **“Export”** are in the
header.

To check a payload against the type, open **Test this type**, choose **Single** or **Array** and
type the value — it is validated as you type.

<Screenshot id="primitive-testing" alt="Test this type: a payload validated against the type, with the problems found" />

### See what uses a type

Before you change a type, check what depends on it. **Scroll down** a type's page to two cards:

<Screenshot id="primitive-detail-used-by-properties" alt="The Dependents table with three referencing types, and the Used by properties table with two bound class properties" />

- **Dependents** has one row for each `$ref` from another type to this one: the referencing type
  (click it to open it), the **Property** the `$ref` sits on (a dash when the whole type is a
  reference), and its **Scope** — **System · core** or **Tenant · *your workspace***. A type that
  references this one from two properties has two rows.
- **Used by properties** has one row for each class property bound to this type — the ones whose
  **Primitive** you chose in the Designer: the property as `Class.property` (click it to open that
  version in the Designer; without Designer access it is plain text), its **Project · Version**,
  and the registry `$ref` it is **Bound as**.

**Used by properties** covers only your workspace's projects: a system type is shared by every
workspace, but you never see another workspace's properties. Properties in deleted classes,
versions or projects are left out. When nothing is bound, the card reads **No property in your
projects uses this type**.

The **Properties** figure under **Used in** is the type's running binding count, so it can be
higher than the list: it also counts bindings removed since, and a system type's bindings in other
workspaces.

## Create a type

1. **Click “Create primitive”** (or press <Kbd keys="N"/>).
2. On **Form**, enter a **Name** (for example `currency-code`) and choose its **Type** (`string`);
   the type cannot change after you create it.
3. Add a **Description**, **Tags**, constraints (format, pattern, length), **Allowed values (enum)**,
   a **Default value** and **Examples**. The **Schema preview** at the bottom shows the result.
   **Advanced JSON** edits the schema directly.
4. **Click “Create”.**

<Screenshot id="primitives-editor" alt="The Create primitive dialog: name, type, description, string constraints, allowed values, default and examples" />

## Import types

Importing brings types you already have into the registry instead of retyping them. One import can
create many types, and the types keep pointing at each other afterwards.

### When to import {#when-to-import-types}

- You have a **JSON Schema 2020-12** document — one schema, or one with reusable types under
  `$defs` (or the older `definitions`).
- You have an **Apiome type-definition bundle**: one `.json` or `.yaml` file holding many types
  under `types`.
- You want the reusable types of an **OpenAPI 3.1** description — its `components/schemas`.

To add a single new type by hand, [create it](#create-a-type) instead.

### Import at a glance {#import-types-at-a-glance}

| Step | Where | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Choose what you are importing | **Source** step, **Source type** | [Source types](#import-source-types) |
| Give the document | **Source** step: **File**, **URL** or **Paste** | [Run an import](#run-an-import) |
| Choose where the types go | **Target namespace (optional)** | [Namespaces & scopes](#namespaces--scopes) |
| Keep references working | Done for you when the types are saved | [How references are kept](#how-import-keeps-references) |
| Settle clashes with existing types | **Review** step | [Review and conflicts](#import-review-and-conflicts) |
| Read what happened | **Result** step | [The result](#the-import-result) |
| Do it without the screen | REST API | [Import with the API](#import-types-with-the-api) |

### Source types {#import-source-types}

| Source type | What becomes a type |
| --- | --- |
| **JSON Schema** | Each entry under `$defs` or `definitions`. A document with neither is imported as one type. |
| **Type-def bundle** | Each entry under `types` (or `$defs` / `definitions`). A bundle of 12 types imports 12 types. |
| **OpenAPI** | Each entry under `components/schemas` — see [From an OpenAPI 3.1 document](#from-an-openapi-31-document). |

Every type is checked as a JSON Schema 2020-12 schema before it is saved.

### Run an import {#run-an-import}

**Click “Import from schema”** (or press <Kbd keys="I"/>). The **Import primitives** dialog has
three steps: **Source**, **Review** and **Result**.

1. **Source** — under **Source type**, choose **JSON Schema**, **Type-def bundle** or **OpenAPI**.
   Then give the document as a **File** (`.json`, `.yaml` or `.yml`), a **URL** or **Paste**.
2. Under **Options**, enter a **Target namespace (optional)** if the types should not go to the
   default one, or tick **Always extract namespace automatically** to take it from the document.
   Two more options are ticked to begin with:
   - **Map recognized formats to core JSON System types** — see
     [How references are kept](#how-import-keeps-references).
   - **Skip definitions identical to an existing type** — see
     [Review and conflicts](#import-review-and-conflicts).
3. **Review** — Apiome lists the types it found. Untick any you do not want, and for each one that
   clashes with an existing type choose **Keep existing**, **Overwrite** or **Import as new name**.
4. **Click “Import N selected”**, then read the **Result** and **click “Done”**.

<Screenshot id="primitives-import" alt="The Import primitives dialog on its Source step: source types, file, URL or paste, and namespace options" />

### How references are kept {#how-import-keeps-references}

Inside a source document, types point at each other with references that only mean something in
that document, such as `#/$defs/Money`. When the types are saved, Apiome rewrites each of these to a
relative reference to the saved type:

| In the source | In the registry |
| --- | --- |
| `#/$defs/Money` | `./money` |
| `#/definitions/Money` | `./money` |
| `#/types/Money` | `./money` |
| `#/components/schemas/Money` | `./money` |
| `#/$defs/Money/properties/amount` | `./money#/properties/amount` |

Relative references keep working when a namespace moves to another base URI, and the
[Resolver](#resolver) follows them like any other `$ref`.

With **Map recognized formats to core JSON System types** ticked, a string that only says
`"format": "email"` (or `uuid`, `uri`, `date`, `date-time`, `time`) is also pointed at the matching
core system type, so every imported email is the same type. A `$ref` you wrote yourself is never
replaced.

### Review and conflicts {#import-review-and-conflicts}

The **Review** step shows what the import would do before anything is saved. Each type has one
status:

| Status | Meaning | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **New** | No type with this name exists in the target namespace. | It is created. |
| **Identical** | The same type is already there. | It is skipped, while **Skip definitions identical to an existing type** is ticked. |
| **Conflict** | A type with this name exists and differs. | You choose — see below. |
| **Invalid** | It is not a valid JSON Schema 2020-12 schema. | It cannot be imported; the row lists what is wrong. |

For a **Conflict**, choose one:

- **Keep existing** — the type in the registry stays as it is. This is the default, so an import
  never replaces a type unless you say so.
- **Overwrite** — the type in the registry is replaced by the imported one.
- **Import as new name** — the imported type is saved beside the existing one under the name you
  enter.

A type that points at something Apiome cannot find is marked as having an unresolved reference. It
still imports; fix the reference later on the **Resolver** tab.

### The result {#the-import-result}

The **Result** step counts the types under **Imported**, **Overwritten**, **Renamed**, **Identical
(skipped)**, **Skipped** and **Errors**. A conflict you left on **Keep existing** is under
**Skipped**. Every import is recorded: the last eight are under **Recent activity** on the
**Registry** tab, and the **imported schemas** count in the facts line goes up.

### From an OpenAPI 3.1 document

Choose **OpenAPI** to import the reusable types of an API description. Each entry under
`components/schemas` becomes one type, named after its component; the document's `info`, `paths`
and other components are not types and are left out.

- **References.** A `$ref` to another component, such as `#/components/schemas/Money`, is rewritten
  to a reference to that type in the registry (`./money`), so the imported types still point at
  each other. A reference to a type arriving in the same import is not reported as unresolved.
- **Versions.** OpenAPI 3.1 schemas are JSON Schema 2020-12, so they are validated as written. An
  OpenAPI 3.0 document still imports, with a warning that 3.0-only keywords may not validate. A
  `jsonSchemaDialect` other than 2020-12 is warned about too.
- **Not OpenAPI.** A document with no `openapi` version, with a version other than 3.x, or with no
  `components/schemas` is refused with a message saying why. A Swagger 2.0 document keeps its types
  under `definitions`: import it as **JSON Schema** instead.

## Namespaces & scopes

A **namespace** groups types under a base URI and version, such as `tenant/acme/v1/types`. The tab
shows the system root and your tenant namespaces, and the order a `$ref` is resolved in: your tenant
namespace, then imported vendor namespaces, then the core system types.

**Click “New namespace”** and enter a **Namespace path**, **Base URI**, **Version root** and
**Description**; tick **Default namespace** to make new types land there. System namespaces are
**Read-only**.

<Screenshot id="primitives-namespaces" alt="Namespaces & scopes: the system root, tenant namespaces, the namespaces table and the resolution order" />

## Resolver

The **Resolver** shows how every `$ref` in your types resolves — **Resolved**, **Unresolved** or
**Circular** — as a list and a reference graph. Filter by **Namespace**, and **click
“Re-resolve”** after fixing a reference.

<Screenshot id="primitives-resolver" alt="The Resolver tab: resolution base, reference graph and the list of references with their status" />

## Settings

**Settings** chooses the **JSON Schema dialect**, how references resolve (the base URL and `$ref`
style), **Import defaults** and **Validation & publishing** rules for this tenant. **Click “Save
settings”**, or **“Reset to defaults”**.

<Screenshot id="primitives-settings" alt="The Settings tab: registry storage, JSON Schema dialect, validation switches and reference resolution" />

## With the CLI or the API

- CLI: `apiome types list|show|search` — see the [CLI quick-start](../reference/cli-quickstart.md).
- REST: `GET` / `POST /v1/primitives/{tenant}`, `GET /v1/primitives/{tenant}/{id}` (with
  `dependents` and `property_dependents`), `GET` / `POST /v1/types/{tenant}/namespaces`,
  `GET` / `PUT /v1/types/{tenant}/settings`, `POST /v1/types/{tenant}/resolve` — see the
  [API reference](../reference/api-reference.md).

### Import types with the API {#import-types-with-the-api}

The dialog uses the same endpoints, so an API import gives the same result. All of them are on the
[Primitives REST reference](../reference/rest/primitives.md).

| Call | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /v1/primitives/{tenant}/import/review` | Dry run: returns each type's status, validation report and reference rewrites. Saves nothing. |
| `POST /v1/primitives/{tenant}/import` | Saves the types and returns the report with an `import_id`. |
| `POST /v1/primitives/{tenant}/import/stage` | Fetches and parses a source — pasted text, a file's text, a URL, or a file in a public GitHub repository — and lists the types it found. Saves no types. |
| `GET /v1/primitives/{tenant}/imports` | Lists past imports. |
| `GET /v1/primitives/{tenant}/imports/{import_id}` | One past import, with its report. |

In the body of `/import/review` and `/import`:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `schema` | The document, as JSON. |
| `source_kind` | `json-schema` (the default), `type-def-bundle` or `openapi`. |
| `import_all` / `selected_definitions` | Import every type, or only the named ones. |
| `target_namespace` | The namespace the types go to. |
| `map_core_formats` | `true` by default — see [How references are kept](#how-import-keeps-references). |
| `dedupe` | `true` by default: an identical type is skipped. |
| `resolutions` | For `/import` only. One entry for each conflicting type: `{"action": "keep"}`, `{"action": "overwrite"}` or `{"action": "rename", "new_name": "money-v2"}`. |

Review needs permission to view types; importing and staging need permission to create them.
